summary: Built and probed the multi-voter variant that question-0 listed as unwitnessed. A three-voter cluster takes one deliberate snapshot (automatic snapshots disabled so no newer snapshot can cover the change), grows to five voters via two added nodes, and the leading node is restarted from its own stores: with RestoreCommittedLogs on it returns holding the snapshot's bootstrap configuration at index 1 with three servers while its own log's latest configuration is index 14 with five servers, and the flag-off control keeps index 14 with five servers; the pre-restart state was index 14 with five servers in both modes, so the membership change committed in both. That is recorded as a child question of the parent configuration-loss question, with the harness and its two comparisons submitted for a receipt. A second consequence was attempted in the same harness — isolating the restarted node with one committed voter while the remaining three voters keep a majority of the committed five — and it did not emerge: the restarted node never reached Leader in either mode (became_leader false, majority_side_leader true, reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3), so an election won with a minority of the committed configuration is explicitly not claimed and is retained as an exploratory negative with its operands. The interpretation is conditional with defect_claim asserted pending the receipt.
